title: Hardware-tailored kernel selection and attention scheduling for multi-GPU tenants
creator: Maya Chen
description: Spike and implementation work to make the inference runtime automatically pick best-performing kernels and scheduling policies for attention-heavy workloads on H100, L40S and A10 hardware. Includes: (1) microbenchmarks for candidate kernels (vendor libraries, Triton/CUTLASS-based fused kernels, and our custom fused-attention), (2) per-GPU profile tables for kernel choice and clock hints, (3) prefill vs decode scheduling policy that minimizes p99 decode latency while keeping prefill throughput efficient, and (4) experiments with MIG partitions on H100 and isolation alternatives on A10/L40S.
acceptance_criteria: Automated kernel-selection table generated for H100/L40S/A10 and loaded at runtime
Decode p99 latency improved >=10% on H100 for medium (2-4 token) decoding workloads under production traffic mix
Prefill throughput drop <=5% when using decode-optimized scheduling in mixed workloads
MIG partitioning playbook for H100 with recommended slice sizes and clock settings documented
Benchmarks and PRs with unit/integration tests merged into runtime-1.22 branch
work_log: 2025-02-12: Kickoff spike defined. Focus areas: fused attention kernels, TFlops vs memory bound ops, clock-frequency tradeoffs, MIG partition experiments on H100 infra.

2025-02-16: Microbenchmark harness completed for QKV fused (FP16) vs vendor flash-attention vs Triton-fused kernels. Initial run on H100: custom fused gives +18% prefill throughput at sequence length 2048 vs vanilla Triton kernels.
2025-02-19: L40S baseline run: vendor kernels are strong at low sequence lengths, but our fused kernels outperform at long sequences (>=1024) by ~12% with lower memory spill.

2025-02-22: A10 notes: no MIG available. We tested process-isolation + cgroups and saw decode p99 tail increases when co-locating heavy prefill workloads; recommend tenant isolation rules for A10 until further GPU-level isolation available.

2025-02-25: Clock tuning: short experiments applying sustained SM GPU clocks on H100 improved decode p99 by 8-12% for small-batch decode but increased energy draw. Decided to expose clock_hint in kernel profile rather than force global changes.

2025-02-28: MIG experiments on H100: 1g.10gb slice for decode-heavy tenants gave best p99 latency isolation while keeping prefill tenants on larger slices. Documented slice sizes and observed throughput numbers.

2025-03-02: Prefill/decode scheduling policy implemented in runtime: dynamic route that sends short decode requests to low-latency MIG slices or accelerated kernel path; long prefill goes to batch-optimized pools. Local perf test shows decode p99 -15% and prefill throughput -3%.

2025-03-03: Code review feedback received from runtime team: add fallback heuristics when kernel selection table has missing entries; add telemetry to detect mis-selection in prod. Incorporating changes.
Links: Confluence spike doc, PRD, perf dashboards and PRs included below.
decisions: Adopt hybrid kernel-selection strategy: prefer vendor-optimized kernels at short seq lengths, use custom fused kernels for long sequences and when KV layout reduces memory traffic
Expose GPU clock_hint per model profile but do NOT enforce cluster-wide clock changes automatically (operator approval required)
Use MIG partitioning for H100 in multi-tenant environments for latency-sensitive tenants; on A10/L40S rely on process isolation and runtime scheduling rules
Implement telemetry hooks to capture kernel_choice, sequence_length, tokens_emitted, and p99 latency for online tuning
open_risks: Sustained higher clocks increase power/cost; need finance impact analysis if we push clock hints by default
MIG availability varies by cloud region and SKU; fallback policies must be robust and observable
Kernel selection adds complexity; incorrect selection could regress latency for some tail cases — telemetry and safe rollback critical
next_steps: Address code review: add missing-entry fallback and simple ML-based override for kernel selection (rule-based first)
Run a 48h canary in staging with production traffic replay: collect kernel-selection telemetry and perf deltas
Finalize MIG playbook and update Dedicated documentation + operator runbook
Merge PRs for runtime-1.22 and schedule release-run verification
